5. The short fact relevant in Writ Petition No. 1537 of 1992 is that respondent No. 2 with intent to purchase better land at suitable place being the exclusive owner and possession of the case land measuring .45 acres of land recorded in R.O.R. Plot No. 43 and 44 of Khatian No. 8 of Mouja Sonkduda, Upazila the petitioner at a price of Tk. 24,000/- which was the market price. The petitioner agreed to purchase the same for which an agreement for sale was executed and registered in favour of the petitioner on receipt of Tk. 10,000/- by the respondent No. 2 as advance towards the consideration money on 8.5.83 with a promise to execute and registrar the sale deed by mid Chaitra, 1992 B.S. after receiving the balance consideration money amounting to Tk. 14,000/-. The copy of the said agreement is annexed as annexure-A. Subsequently respondent vendor approached the petitioner saying that he would purchase some other more profitable land for which he was in urgent need of Tk. 20.000/- in place of balance of Tk. 14,000/- and if the petitioner is in a position to pay the same he would at once execute the sale deed and hand over possession of the selfsame .45 acres of land. Accordingly the petitioner to avoid complications agreed to pay the increased consideration money to the tune of Tk. 30,000/- in place of earlier fixed price of Tk. 24,000/-. So the respondent No. 2 on receipt of the balance of Tk. 20,000/- executed and registered the sale deed being deed No. 19319 dated 9.10.83 annexed to the petition as annexure-B and handed over possession within the knowledge of all concerned and the respondent requested the petitioner to execute the deed agreement for re conveyance in favour of respondent No. 2 with a promise that he would recover the case land within Bhadra 1333 B.S. in case of failing to pay the consideration money kabala would be treated as an out and out sale forfeiting the right of re conveyance. A true copy of the agreement is annexed hereto an annexure-C. After purchase the petitioner developed the same for cultivation and mutated his name without any objection from any corner and opened a separate Khatian No. 222 at the yearly rent of Tk. 2.25 along with the other purchased land necessary .45 acres from the vendor. The Mutation Case No. 1495 (IX-1) and the D.C.R. annexed hereto as annexures-D and E respectfully. While thus enjoying the land by growing crops the respondent No. 2 filed a case being No. 152/89-90 under section 11 of the Bangladesh Rin Shalishi Act, 1989 (Act 15. of 1989) before the Chairman Upazila Rin Shalishi Board alleging falsely that he took Tk. 48.000/- as loan from the petitioner against the said land along with another land for an amount of Tk. 18,000/- to be repaid by the petitioner. Petitioner, on receipt of the notice from the Rin Shalishi Board filed written objection against the same denying all the allegations as false, concocted and highly malafide and after hearing the case in presence of both the parties the Board dismissed the case on 30.7.90. As against that respondent No. 2 preferred an appeal being No. 21 (XIX) of 1990 to the Appellate Authority i.e. the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev) Jamalpur who after hearing and considering the materials on records rejected the same affirming the order of the Chairman, Upazila Rin Shalishi Board by his order dated 20.1.91. The photo copy of the application, the dismissal and Appellate order are annexed annexures-F.G and 

 6. The relevant fact in Writ Petition No. 1751/92 is that the respondent No. 2 to purchase better land at a suitable place being the exclusive owner and possession of the case land measuring an area of .30 acres in C.S. Plot No. 20 corresponding to R.O.R. Plot No. 43 and 44 of C.S. Khatian No. 4 corresponding to R.O.R. Khatian No. 8 of Mouza Sonkada Upazila Sadar, Jamalpur District proposed to sell the same to the petitioner at the market price amounting to Tk. 18,000/-. The petitioner agreed to purchase the same and the respondent No. 2 on receipt of the price of Tk. 18,000/- executed a sale deed. The photo copy of the same is annexed as Annexure-A. In terms of the sale deed the vendor respondent No. 2 handed over the possession to the petitioner within the knowledge of all concerned and then the respondent requested the petitioner to execute a deed of agreement for re conveyance with a promise that he would recover the case land within 2 years 11 months and in case of failure to pay the consideration money the kabala would be treated as an out of out sale forfeiting the right of re conveyance. Photo copy of the same is annexed an Annexure-Al. The petitioner after purchase developed the land and mutated his name without any objection and opened a separate Khatian No. 222 at yearly rent of Tk 2.25 along with the purchased land of .30 decimals including other purchased land necessary .45 acres from the same vendor in Mutation Case No. 1495(IX-1). The mutation khs.1".....1 and the duplicate carbon receipt are annexed as Annexure B and C respectively. While the petitioner possessing the same respondent No, 2 filed a case in respect of 2 different purchase deeds being case No. 152/89-90 under section 11 of Bangladesh Rin Shalishi Act 1989 (Act 15 of 1989) before the Chairman Upazila Rin Shalishi Board alleging that he took loan from the petitioner amounting to Tk. 18,000/- and for another deed an amount of Tk. 50,000/- to be repaid to the petitioner by installments. On receipt of the notice the petitioner appeared and filed written objection denying all allegations contending that those were false, concocted and highly malafide and after hearing both the parties the Rin Shalishi Board dismissed the same on 30.7.90. Against which respondent No. 2 preferred an appeal being No. 21 (XIX) of 1990 to the Appellate Authority, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Jamalpur who after perusing the materials on record dis-missed the appeal upholding the order of the Rin Shalishi Board by his order dated 20.1.91. The petitioner order of the Board and the dismissal order are annexed as Annexure-D and E and F respectively. Thereafter respondent No. 2 filed a case being No. 70(4)91 in the court of the Upazila Magistrate under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act praying for redemption of the mortgaged land and restoration of possession of the same. The true copy of the same is annexed as Annexure-G. Petitioner filed written objection against the same before the Upazila Magistrate denying the allegations as an illegal claim. True copy of the same is annexed as Annexure-H. The learned Upazila Magistrate allowed the redemption case and directed the petitioner to handover possession within 15 days by his order dated 9.3.92. The certified copy of the same is annexed as Annexure-I.
